model.rationale: DeLauro combines durable incumbency, a district leaning Democratic by eight points, and a fundraising edge of more than a hundred-to-one, leaving Lancia without visible resources or a demonstrated path. Markets price her re-election near certain, and nothing in the available evidence points the other way.
model.watch: With no public polling, a late-breaking scandal or a sharply unfavorable national environment for Democrats would be the main ways this race could tighten.

overview:
Rosa DeLauro seeks another term in this New Haven-area district, which leans Democratic by eight points on the partisan index. She has raised about $1.56 million this cycle with roughly $194,000 on hand, while Republican Chris Lancia has raised about $14,600 with under $5,000 available. An independent candidate, Thomas Egan, is also on the ballot but reports no fundraising. No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets price DeLauro's re-election around 96 percent, and the underlying fundamentals point the same way: incumbency, a vast financial advantage, and a favorable district. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the exact size of the winning margin open, though the direction of the race is not in serious doubt.
